Mina the hollower isn't really the top down Zelda game its advertised to be it would be  best described as a top down souls borne like game with heavy emphasis on platforming.  The game has a stellar combat sandbox and all the bosses and platforming is surprisingly decent too considering the game mimics 2d Zelda but the dungeons in the game are missing the puzzle design i would want from a game so clearly inspired by those older Nintendo games as a substitute the game does have some minor puzzles and secrets in the over world but i would've just liked to see way more of them especially in the dungeons. Besides disappointing me in the aspect yacht club still have a fantastic game on their hands everything they set out to do with this game has been accomplished exceptionally well.

Planet of Lana II is a fun and whimsical romp though a gorgeous alien planet. While the first game is more memorable and unique in terms of narrative, this sequel is not disappointing, and carries on a more action-focused traditional plot. The game is chill with simplistic gameplay. It's a wonderful way to wind down an evening. The music and art-direction are quite literally out-of-this-world. I recommend this game to anyone searching for a relaxing and beautiful time, while still looking for some narrative substance.

One of my favourite games of this decade, No, I'm not a Human does a stellar job of creating a sense of fear, doubt, and existential dread. The numerous eccentric characters and endings make the game highly replayable, and the disconcerting art style supplements the ever-present sense of distrust and unease. The melancholic soundtrack is legitimately iconic. I particularly appreciate the quiet introspective moments you can spend looking out the window each night, watching helplessly as the world outside slowly descends into chaos.

I have loved this game, it feels like someone has played Manhunt and Condemned, and said "hey let's make a game that has a story inspired by Manhunt and gameplay like Condemned and give the players an option to interact with the props on the environment to fight the enemies like Half-Life 2. It felt like it took some of the best elements from some games. I recommend this if you like Manhunt and Condemned, and survival horror games in general.
Also thanks cop_fighter for gifting me this game on his own birthday!

IDK, and I'm not sure I ever will, but I'm enjoying the adventure, what more could I ask for?
